prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring chosen proteins and E3 ubiquitin ligases together so that the cell destroys the target

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from halide perovskites (B066) to targeted protein degradation (B027). My test is whether a mechanism was actually established with structural and biochemical evidence and then confirmed by many independent groups. Degradation by induced proximity meets it: a small molecule that holds a target and an E3 ligase together was demonstrated in vitro and in cells, and the cereblon finding gives the thalidomide-type glue branch a molecular explanation that can be written into a citation. It is a new chemical modality and a general one, and the concept is shared across a broad community. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Together the three cover both branches within the three-name limit.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved as far as I know, and my clinical statements are from memory and unverified. A committee that wants durable interpretation could reasonably wait. Credit is crowded: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray all have real claims, and one citation spanning PROTACs and cereblon glues may merge two discoveries made by different groups at different times. I also give up the perovskite case, which I still think is scientifically strong, because it found no support in round 1 and the stability, lead and credit objections are not answered by my arguments alone.

responses.point: Linke moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa, but still worries that one citation merges the PROTAC and cereblon-glue discoveries, and that no degrader is clearly approved.
responses.response: In round 1 I asked you to settle the PROTAC versus cereblon split before I could treat B027 as the leader. Your answer persuades me that a single citation framed on the shared principle, recruiting an E3 ligase to a chosen target, is more honest than a narrower citation, provided the wording says induced proximity and does not claim one modality. On timing I agree with you that clinical status is unverified. I now weigh the confirmed mechanism and independent reproduction more heavily than approval, as I argued for perovskites. I accept that the omission of Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made degraders drug-like, is the real cost of this trio.

responses.point: Chabes supports B027 only as a second part, with Crews and Handa but not Deshaies, paired with Liu's base editing (B038).
responses.response: I would keep Deshaies. A citation about E3 ligase recruitment that leaves out one of the two people who conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional concept would be hard to defend, and Crews and Handa alone would not stand on the same footing as the PROTAC trio the others have converged on. I also prefer one coherent achievement to a two-part prize that pairs fields because the three-person cap forces it. Base editing is clean for Liu, but the 2020 CRISPR prize makes it read as a follow-on, and a short clinical record argues for waiting. If the committee does want a second part, I would look for a structural or materials achievement rather than another medicine-facing one.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that Crews, Deshaies and Handa cover both the heterobifunctional and glue branches inside the three-person limit, and that B027 is the most plausible place to converge.
responses.response: I agree on the mapping of names to branches, and my change of position rests on it. I disagree that broad opening support settles the question. Four of eight is not a majority and counts do not replace the science. My reasons are that the mechanism is established and reproduced, and that cereblon gives a structurally anchored explanation of the glue chemistry. I do not share your confidence about clinical consequences, since you cite many trials but no approval and none of us has checked the record. I would keep the clinical claim out of the citation.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved from B026 to B027 and asks whether PROTACs and cereblon-based glues are one achievement or two, which determines whether Handa belongs in the same citation.
responses.response: I think they are one achievement at the level of principle and two histories at the level of discovery. What unites them is E3 ligase recruitment by a small molecule leading to ubiquitination and proteasomal removal. The cereblon work is what shows, at a molecular level, that this is how glue degraders operate, so Handa belongs in the citation. I agree the expert reports are the right place to test that reading, and I rely on your reading of them, since I have not seen them in this round. If the reports show that the glue branch is a separate achievement, I would still prefer this trio to splitting the credit further.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli should replace Deshaies or Handa if the committee weights drug-like degrader design and ternary-complex structure more heavily; I cannot resolve this from the round-1 statements alone.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes B027 premature this year; clinical status is from memory and unverified.
Whether perovskites (B066) deserve renewed consideration in a later year once stability and credit are clearer; my own change of preference is partly a response to the lack of support.
Whether a single citation can cover the PROTAC and cereblon-glue branches without conflating two discoveries.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict or recusal need is apparent for Crews, Deshaies or Handa, or for the perovskite and nitrogenase alternatives. My field is 3D electron diffraction for nanocrystals, which is adjacent to serial femtosecond crystallography (B002), so I would treat that ballot cautiously and defer to colleagues on attribution there; B002 is not in my configuration. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, which has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate.
